races.name: Melissa, Arabella And Oriana Hawthorne Handicap

runners_data.name: Keats House
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner in this field, she sets the entire race shape; Good ground at Musselburgh is fine (12 sim-going runs, 1W5P) and the 1m1f trip is within her range, though a STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) signals she is technically racing out of role — if her lead is unchallenged she may last longer than her overall form suggests.

runners_data.name: Mayor Of Maghera
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope takes the ride for R Mike Smith, a combination worth noting; this 4yo has placed at 9f on Good and the step up from 8f could unlock improvement, with a hood previously worn suggesting he needs some settling — he is a genuine prominent-to-hold-up type and the slower pace may test his ability to quicken.

runners_data.name: Perfidia
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's consistent filly returns just five days after her last run and has a strong Good-ground record (12/15, 2W8P); her true style is hold-up but, with three genuine closers for only a handful of rear slots, she is likely to be further forward than ideal — the 1m1f is a touch further than her 7-8f form, which may stretch her stamina slightly.

runners_data.name: Without Delay
runners_data.note: Tracy Waggott's 7yo arrives after a 40-day break — the longest layoff in this field — which is a notable fitness concern; a natural hold-up horse who has placed at 7f on Good, she will likely find herself racing in an unnatural midfield position and the combination of the step up to 1m1f and the break may see her find the trip beyond her best.

runners_data.name: Approaching Dawn
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's 6yo is lightly handicapped at OR 46 and showed a win at 8f on Good recently (1/8f/GOO); she is a true hold-up horse by inclination but redistribution may force her to race closer than she wants — Lauren Young's 5lb claim is an asset, and if she can secure a genuine rear pitch she holds more tactical credibility than the others mapped similarly.

runners_data.name: Bay Dream Believer
runners_data.note: Jason Hart rides this 7yo who has a solid record at 10f on Good (1W, multiple places) but is stepping down to 1m1f — the trip reduction is the primary concern, as her best form has come over a longer trip where she can use her stamina; T14 of 0/21 for Mark Walford hints the stable is not in the deepest form, and headgear (h) is worth monitoring if she switches off.

runners_data.name: Second Fiddle
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's 7yo is a prominent-tracking type by profile but has not won or placed in recent 8-9f Good-ground outings (sim-going 0W0P in 5 tries), which is a blunt negative; Aiden Brookes takes the ride and the horse's consistent finish positions of 4th-10th suggest a runner who gets into races without threatening — the headgear (t, tongue tie) is retained but has not unlocked improvement.

races.paceDynamic: Keats House is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead among the seven runners, is set to dictate from the front at a sustainable, controlled tempo over this 1m1f Musselburgh trip on Good ground. Second Fiddle carries a prominent tag and may attempt to press, but has a poor recent record at this level and is unlikely to apply significant pressure, leaving Keats House to bowl along unchallenged and set a rhythm entirely of her choosing. The three hold-up types — Perfidia, Without Delay, and Approaching Dawn — are genuinely back-end horses who cannot all find their natural position at the rear given the limited early pace in this race, meaning at least two of them will be shuffled into a midfield role that dilutes their true tactical identity. This moderate, uncontested gallop strongly favours prominent racers who can track the leader and pounce from a position of comfort, rather than deep closers who rely on a stronger pace to set up their finish.

scenarios.title: Keats House Controls Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If Keats House leads unchallenged and the pace stays honest without collapse, allowing prominent challengers to sustain their run.
scenarios.body: If Keats House leads unchallenged and the pace stays honest without collapse, allowing prominent challengers to sustain their run.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Close Pursuer Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent-tracking horse settles just off the pace and produces a well-timed challenge in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If a prominent-tracking horse settles just off the pace and produces a well-timed challenge in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Delivers Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is brisk enough to string the field out and leave a genuine gap for a closer to run through.
scenarios.body: If the pace is brisk enough to string the field out and leave a genuine gap for a closer to run through.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Collapse Of Pace, Blanket Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Keats House crawls early and the field concertinas approaching the home turn, producing a sprint-finish scramble.
scenarios.body: If Keats House crawls early and the field concertinas approaching the home turn, producing a sprint-finish scramble.

watchPoints.text: Keats House is the sole front-runner and if she overcomes her STYLE_FIT flag to lead unchallenged at a fair clip, the entire race revolves around whether she can be caught — watch whether Second Fiddle attempts to press her early, which would be the only pace threat.

Perfidia, Without Delay, and Approaching Dawn are all genuine hold-up types forced into midfield by field congestion at the rear — if any of them is caught wide and unable to settle, their finishing kick will be blunted and their chance effectively gone.

Without Delay has not run for 40 days — the longest absence in this field — and Tracy Waggott's T14 of 0/6 provides no warm stable form to offset the fitness query; watch her in the paddock and monitor early market moves.

Bay Dream Believer is stepping down from 10f, where all her best form is concentrated, to 1m1f — if the pace collapses she could stay on, but she will need the race to set up for her in a way that this race shape makes unlikely.

Daniel Tudhope on Mayor Of Maghera is the most significant jockey booking in the race — Tudhope's course knowledge at Musselburgh is considerable and his ability to find cover and time a run from a prominent position could prove decisive if the race unfolds at a steady tempo.

races.name: Join Racing TV Now Handicap

runners_data.name: Marhaba Ghaiyyath
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed pace-setter, expected to lead and dictate throughout; Charlie Johnston yard is in decent form (9/67 over 14 days), but 59 days off and a patchy recent record (80-650) raise fitness questions — its best role is pace-maker here with a style-fit caveat.

runners_data.name: High Degree
runners_data.note: William Haggas-trained 4yo back after just 17 days, consistent in similar going (6/8 on good), has placed over 10f on good ground and looks ideally positioned to track the leader and kick; compact profile suits this controlled shape.

runners_data.name: Two B Tanned
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on good going and arrives with headgear (hp) that may sharpen focus; Julie Camacho runner back after 54 days, has shown versatility across going types — the step up to 9f here is a query but the on-pace style suits the expected race development.

runners_data.name: Pandemonium
runners_data.note: Sharp 3yo who broke well to win at 7f and 8f on soft — genuinely wants to race up with the pace but is catalogued to midfield because of a congested front rank; the style mismatch depresses its chance, and it may need a messy race to find its natural position.

runners_data.name: Strength Of Spirit
runners_data.note: Busy recent profile (two runs in 24 days), won over 8f on soft and placed on good — a true prominent racer whose instinct to bowl along freely has been squeezed out by the race shape; K R Burke in form (9/51), but this horse needs to be prominent to be seen at its best and cannot guarantee that here.

runners_data.name: Dwindling Funds
runners_data.note: Front-rank operator at heart, placed over 8-10f on good and soft, but the congested early positions mean it is catalogued to midfield — ran only 11 days ago so fitness is fine, yet Jim Goldie's runner faces a tactical puzzle it may struggle to resolve given the available positions.

runners_data.name: Monoceros
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on good for Iain Jardine and has placed at 8f on soft; genuinely wants to race prominently but will find its ground occupied — in a less crowded race this horse would be much more dangerous; keep expectations modest given the structural disadvantage.

runners_data.name: Haayimm
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 3yo with Edward Bethell, won over 8f on soft and placed on good — only three career runs but the form trajectory is encouraging; Daniel Tudhope in the saddle is a major positive at Musselburgh and a 58-day break is not a concern for a yard that places horses carefully.

runners_data.name: Rochfortbridge
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse and the most naturally suited to late delivery — course form is limited (0W0P on good), has not run for 94 days and the trip is a slight query, but if pace collapse or traffic drama materialises this is the right profile to benefit.

runners_data.name: Thunder Wonder
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's second string, a true hold-up type who rarely threatens early; 11/15 finishing position on good going is a sobering stat, 59 days off mirrors stablemate, and the recent form string (00-048) inspires little confidence — needs everything to go right.

races.paceDynamic: Marhaba Ghaiyyath is the sole confirmed front-runner and should lead comfortably from the outset, setting a measured, uncontested gallop over this 1m1f trip on good ground at Musselburgh. With no genuine rival likely to press her early, the pace will be sustainable rather than searching, creating a race that plays directly into the hands of horses who can track the leader closely and kick off the turn. This field contains significantly more prominent-running types than the early positions can accommodate — Strength Of Spirit, Pandemonium, Monoceros, and Dwindling Funds are all natural front-rank horses who will be shuffled back into a midfield they do not naturally occupy, meaning their chance is compromised by race shape rather than ability alone. The tactical verdict is clear: horses who can sit second or third in a controlled race and produce a clean, well-timed challenge off a genuine pace — true prominent or close-tracking types — are best placed to capitalise here.

scenarios.body: If Marhaba Ghaiyyath bowls along at a steady clip and the race develops into a procession before quickening in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.body: If the early gallop is so modest that the field bunches and a late surge from those held up in midfield becomes viable in the final furlong.

scenarios.title: Pace Increases, Front Runs Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Marhaba Ghaiyyath accelerates significantly from halfway and the bunched midfield cannot close the gap.
scenarios.body: If Marhaba Ghaiyyath accelerates significantly from halfway and the bunched midfield cannot close the gap.

scenarios.title: Chaos In Midfield, Outsider Profits
scenarios.trigger: If the bunching of redistributed prominent types causes positional scrimmaging through the first half, allowing a fresh-legged horse to exploit the disorder late.
scenarios.body: If the bunching of redistributed prominent types causes positional scrimmaging through the first half, allowing a fresh-legged horse to exploit the disorder late.

watchPoints.text: Marhaba Ghaiyyath has not run for 59 days and its recent form (80-650) is unconvincing — if it fails to stride on fully, the pace evaporates and the entire race shape shifts.

Strength Of Spirit, Pandemonium and Monoceros will all be hunting the same two or three prominent positions at the start; watch for a congested, pushing early order that disrupts several fancied runners' rhythm.

Haayimm has only three career starts — Daniel Tudhope's course experience is an asset but greenness under pressure in a competitive handicap over a trip slightly beyond anything it has encountered could surface late.

Two B Tanned is fitted with headgear (hp) and returns after 54 days — the hood effect in first-time or reapplied use can sharpen early pace significantly and may influence how aggressively it contests the prominent positions.
Rochfortbridge has not run for 94 days and has never won on good ground — if the hold-up scenario materialises, its fitness and going suitability will both be tested simultaneously.

races.name: Max Recycle Handicap

runners_data.name: Rajstar
runners_data.note: A hold-up specialist with a modest 0W0P from 6 similar-going runs, last seen finishing seventh over 6f on good ground 12 days ago; Ben Haslam is 1/20 over 14 days and the step up to 7f has not produced results — sits furthest back with least tactical flexibility in a race where the pace won't suit deep closers.

runners_data.name: Classy Clarets
runners_data.note: In solid recent form (1W4P in 15 similar-going runs) and finished third last time out over this course and distance on good ground — naturally a hold-up horse but, with so many closers in the field, will likely find himself racing in midfield rather than off the pace, which partially suits a more prominent campaign.

runners_data.name: Defence Missile
runners_data.note: Difficult to fancy on the evidence: just one win-or-place in 12 similar-going runs, trainer Linda Perratt 0/4 over 14 days, and his natural closing style is further compromised by being pushed into midfield where he lacks the profile to dominate; recent form (8-6-8-5-11) reinforces the concern.

runners_data.name: Cotai Starlight
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old on a 69-day break, carrying just 132lbs, with only 3 runs on similar going (0W0P); Katie Scott's stable is 0/9 over 14 days and the extra distance to 7f is untested in earnest — too many unknowns to trust in this company.

runners_data.name: Willowinghurn
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope is a significant booking for David O'Meara (8/54 T14) and the horse has previously raced prominently (headgear note: p), but 11 of 15 similar-going runs have ended in single-figure finishes and the 16-day turnaround brings modest recent form (9-7-8-5-0); handicap mark of 58 feels optimistic.

runners_data.name: Monhammer
runners_data.note: Veteran at eight years, and while he has placed three times in 15 similar-going outings, his form string of 3-2-5-10-3 is inconsistent; Linda Perratt's 0/4 T14 record and the fact that his natural closing style is being squeezed into midfield both dampen expectations for a horse who needs things to go his way late.

runners_data.name: Due Respect
runners_data.note: Listed as a non-runner — any analysis is academic; the entry should be treated as void for race-shape purposes and the remaining field recalculated accordingly.

runners_data.name: Sanditon
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on standard ground and placed third on good going in his latest start, showing genuine course-and-distance aptitude; inclined to race prominently by inclination though shown here in midfield — the stable (Charlie Johnston, 5/48 T14) and good-ground figures (1/15) urge caution about his chance if the pace doesn't set up.

runners_data.name: Coconut Bay
runners_data.note: Two wins from 15 similar-going appearances is a positive baseline for a seven-year-old, and Jason Hart is a capable pilot, but 10 of those runs have ended outside the places; the horse's hold-up tendencies are genuine but the redistribution into midfield combined with a 22-day absence makes his chance speculative rather than convincing.

runners_data.name: Ramon Di Loria
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed pace-setter; Greg Fairley rides for Ewan Whillans who has a modest 14-day strike rate, but the tactical advantage of uncontested lead on good ground at 7f is enormous here, and his good-going record of 2/15 runs is the critical caveat on how well he converts control into victory.

races.paceDynamic: Ramon Di Loria is the sole confirmed front-runner in this field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will dictate an uncontested, measured gallop over Musselburgh's flat seven furlongs on good ground. The remainder of the field is overwhelmingly composed of hold-up types — Sanditon, Classy Clarets, Defence Missile, Monhammer, Due Respect and Coconut Bay are all natural closers who cannot all occupy their preferred rearward position, meaning several will be pushed into unfamiliar midfield berths against their will. With Ramon Di Loria able to control the tempo from the front without pressure, the race is likely to be run at a sustainable, even pace that suits horses who can travel prominently or make smooth headway from midfield rather than those requiring a strong early gallop to set up a late finish. The field holds considerably more genuine hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — those most likely to secure a rearward position are the true closers with the clearest recent form, such as Classy Clarets and Sanditon, though even they may find the pace insufficient to reel in a relaxed front-runner. This race shape decisively favours a horse that can sit close to the steady pace and quicken from a handy position, with pure hold-up closers at a significant disadvantage given the likely lack of early pressure.

scenarios.title: Ramon Controls, Stays Honest

scenarios.title: Closers Sweep Through Late

watchPoints.text: Ramon Di Loria sets the only pace — watch whether Greg Fairley elects to go fast or dawdle, as the entire complexion of the race hinges on his tempo choice from the front.

Classy Clarets and Sanditon are natural hold-up horses likely to be ridden closer than ideal given the overcrowded rear; watch whether they settle in midfield or get involved in an early positional scramble that costs them late energy.

Cotai Starlight's 69-day absence and limited form base make her a significant unknown — watch the paddock and market for any signs of market confidence from the Katie Scott yard before treating her as a live player.

Due Respect is listed as a non-runner — confirm the final field size before the off, as removing one hold-up type slightly eases the positional congestion at the rear and could marginally improve the closing prospects of those who remain.

Willowinghurn is bred and previously raced to handle a pace-dependent scenario — watch whether Tudhope uses the horse's prominent headgear history to push up closer than the map suggests, which could make him a surprise eyecatcher if the pace picks up.

races.name: Racing TV Profits Returned To Racing Handicap

runners_data.name: Son
runners_data.note: A hold-up performer with solid claims on paper — two consecutive runner-up finishes over this C&D on Good ground for Tim Easterby — but rests on a true gallop materialising, which this pace map does not guarantee.

runners_data.name: Abduction
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's eight-year-old won over 7f Good at this course and has shown C&D form; genuinely needs to come from off the pace and is reliant on the front-runners setting enough of a test to bring him into it.

runners_data.name: Ameilya
runners_data.note: Long absence of 399 days is the dominant concern here; a true hold-up type by style, she has been placed in midfield on the map simply because the field has more rear-division types than slots available, and her distance profile (previously seen over 9-17f) raises a legitimate query at 7f Good.

runners_data.name: Gressington
runners_data.note: Has the headgear of a horse needing a spark — but a form string of 006080 tells its own story; genuinely comes from off the pace but has failed to place in any of his last five starts on Good or equivalent going, making his redistribution to midfield a matter of course rather than opportunity.

runners_data.name: Iris Dancer
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins and consistent blinkers use over 6f Good are encouraging, but she is a true closer whose best form has come over shorter; the step to 7f means she needs the pace to ensure she can deliver her late effort, and in a shape that looks set to suit front-runners, she may find herself making ground without ever quite getting there.

runners_data.name: Diamont Katie
runners_data.note: K R Burke's four-year-old is the race's pacesetter and will dictate the tempo; recent form shows progressive placed efforts stepping up to 7f and she holds strong course-and-distance form figures — this is her natural role and she is the horse the entire field will be measured against.

runners_data.name: Native Instinct
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope takes the ride for Edward Bethell on a horse who ran second over 8f Good and has placed on 7f Good before; the 43-day absence is worth noting but he is a genuine prominent type who will be involved early and should appreciate a true-run 7f.

runners_data.name: The Gay Blade
runners_data.note: The form horse in this field with three wins in his last four — twice over 7f Good including Musselburgh — and Andrew Mullen keeps the ride; he races prominently and the combination of course familiarity, in-form trainer Iain Jardine, and the right style for this race shape makes him a central figure.

races.paceDynamic: Diamont Katie is the lone confirmed front runner and looks set to dictate from the front at a sustainable gallop, with Native Instinct and The Gay Blade likely to press from prominent positions and keep the pace honest without turning it into a burn-up. With only one genuine pace-setter, the tempo should be controlled rather than frantic, meaning the early leaders will not be unduly pressured and the race is unlikely to develop into a true test of stamina or a messy scrimmage. The redistribution flag applies here: Son, Abduction, Ameilya, Gressington, and Iris Dancer are all hold-up types, but with five horses needing to come from off the pace and a relatively small field, true late closers will need to find something significant in the final two furlongs on ground that will not be testing. This race shape — controlled pace set by Diamont Katie, covered up by two prominent types — strongly favours horses with a prominent or pace-pressing profile that can sit close to the action and respond when the tempo quickens, rather than those relying on a strong gallop to reel in the leaders.

scenarios.title: Diamont Katie Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Diamont Katie leads unchallenged and the prominent pair Native Instinct and The Gay Blade track without applying real pressure.
scenarios.body: If Diamont Katie leads unchallenged and the prominent pair Native Instinct and The Gay Blade track without applying real pressure.

scenarios.body: If The Gay Blade or Native Instinct tracks Diamont Katie closely and times a challenge perfectly entering the final two furlongs.

scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected and the closers get a genuine gallop to run at in the straight.
scenarios.body: If the pace is stronger than expected and the closers get a genuine gallop to run at in the straight.

scenarios.title: Chaos From Wide Draw
scenarios.trigger: If a poor start or wayward early running bunches the field and produces a falsely-run or scrappy contest.

watchPoints.text: The Gay Blade has won two of his last three over 7f Good at Musselburgh and his pressing style puts him perfectly placed to challenge Diamont Katie — the pair are on a collision course in the straight.

Ameilya's 399-day absence combined with a previous profile over middle-distances (9-17f) represents a significant unknown; any market move should be treated with caution given the style and fitness questions.

Son is carrying top weight for a hold-up horse in a race with only one genuine front runner — if Diamont Katie controls the pace without being pressed, Son may find too little to aim at coming off the final bend.

Iris Dancer is equipped with blinkers and has won back-to-back over 6f — watch whether Rowan Scott settles her early, because if she races too keenly in a slowly-run 7f she is unlikely to see it out effectively.

Native Instinct reappears after 43 days off for Edward Bethell; Daniel Tudhope's booking is a positive signal but the layoff and a previous tendency to find only 6th over 7f Good is worth monitoring in the market.

races.name: Catherine & Charlotte Roche Handicap

runners_data.name: Gemini Man
runners_data.note: Proven front-runner who has won four of his last five including twice over 12f on Good/Standard, and a bold-jumping Iain Jardine stable in good form (4/34 in 14 days); at 8 years old carrying 139lbs he is fit off an 8-day break and his ability to dominate solo is the defining tactical factor of this race.

runners_data.name: Sophiesticate
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up mare with a modest recent form string of 77-763 and two of her last three outings over the shorter 8f trip; Kyle McHugh's 7lb claim softens the weight burden but her trainer has a blank 14-day record (0/13) and her hold-up style requires more pace ahead than this race is likely to generate.

runners_data.name: Is She Now
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 13f on Soft and David Nolan takes the ride for Daragh Bourke, but her wider form reveals she has struggled badly over 16f and on Good ground recently; a true hold-up type who needs a strong pace to reel in and, with Gemini Man likely to keep things controlled, catching him from off the pace is a tall order.

runners_data.name: Storm On Jura
runners_data.note: Four-year-old who fades in the finish — flagged explicitly in the pace data — and whose best recent efforts have come over shorter trips (8-9f); Jim Goldie's yard is firing (7/37 in 14 days) but Storm On Jura's natural instinct to come from off the pace is undermined by both his tendency to weaken late and the absence of strong gallop to exploit.

runners_data.name: Falaise Blanc
runners_data.note: Consistent placer at this trip on Good ground with two seconds and a fourth in her last four starts over 12-13f, and Jason Hart is a reliable booking; she wears a visor and naturally wants to come from behind, but her form at the distance and going gives her the strongest credentials of the hold-up group should the pace ease enough for closers.

runners_data.name: On The Bubble
runners_data.note: Greg Fairley-ridden five-year-old with six placed efforts in 15 outings on Good ground, suggesting consistency without a win; his best efforts have come over 8-9f rather than this 1m4½f trip, and while a natural hold-up type, the step up in distance and lack of a strong pace to chase makes this a difficult assignment.

races.paceDynamic: Gemini Man is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner field and, with no genuine pace rival to pressure him, he is expected to bowl along at a controlled, sustainable tempo over this 1m4½f trip on Good ground at Musselburgh. With Andrew Mullen aboard a horse that has won four of his last five starts when able to dominate, the fractions will be honest but far from suicidal, meaning the leaders' advantage is unlikely to be surrendered cheaply in the straight. The remainder of the field — Sophiesticate, Is She Now, Storm On Jura, Falaise Blanc and On The Bubble — are all natural hold-up or come-from-behind operators, and with so many closers chasing the same ground late, the finishing kick of the pack will be diluted by competition for running room. This race shape strongly favours the front-running profile: a lone, uncontested pace-setter over a staying trip on a flat, galloping track who never gets headed is the classic scenario where prominent and lead horses convert, and closers find themselves with too much to do against an unexposed tempo-setter. Three horses — Storm On Jura, Falaise Blanc and On The Bubble — are genuine hold-up types pushed forward on the pace map simply because the map cannot place everyone at the rear; none of the six is likely to challenge Gemini Man for the early lead.

scenarios.body: If the congestion among five hold-up horses causes interference or missed runs in the straight, with one to emerge cleanly from the pack.

scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Aids Jockeys

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Andrew Mullen settles Gemini Man immediately — if he bowls along from the off unchallenged, the race is likely to be his from the front and the hold-up pack will struggle to close.

Monitor Falaise Blanc's position tracking into the straight — as the hold-up runner with the most relevant placed form over this trip and going, she is the one most likely to emerge as the danger to Gemini Man if closers fire.

With five hold-up horses chasing limited room in the straight, watch for traffic trouble in the final two furlongs; horses drawn wider or caught on the inside rail could lose momentum at a critical moment.

Storm On Jura's flagged tendency to fade in the finish is worth noting for lay purposes — if he tracks up into a prominent position early, his stamina over this distance on Good ground is an open question.

Is She Now's win last time came on Soft ground over 13f; the switch to Good at Musselburgh over a similar trip is not an automatic negative, but her form on Good in the past 12 months (18th from 18 runners over 18f stands out) warrants caution before upgrading that win.

races.name: Watch On Racing TV Handicap

runners_data.name: Invincible Crown
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer at 5f on good going for Ruth Carr and James Sullivan, returning quickly on just 5 days' rest; only 1 place from 6 runs on similar going suggests she rarely lands the killer blow, and racing off a hot pace she rarely creates is unlikely to change that.

runners_data.name: Auntie Jo
runners_data.note: Won over 5f on standard going for Katie Scott and Jason Hart and placed on good last time, showing live form claims; a genuine hold-up horse placed in midfield by the mapping because the rear is oversubscribed, so she will likely race closer than she wants without it being her natural rhythm.

runners_data.name: Wee Mary
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's filly has course and distance form including a 5f win on good going, and Amie Waugh takes the mount; although her true style is prominent rather than front-running, she is the only horse mapped to the lead and will set terms — the STYLE_FIT tag (0.81) is a mild flag, but she dictates by default.

runners_data.name: Data Fata Secutus
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope rides this Rebecca Menzies three-year-old, whose last run was a 2nd over 5f on good going — solid recent form; a genuine hold-up horse whose historical profile on similar going reads 0W2P, and he will need to find a clear run against a compressed field.

runners_data.name: Gwen Tennyson
runners_data.note: Gemma Tutty's three-year-old has placed over 5f on good ground and returns after 19 days; limited sim-going data (1/4) makes her something of a wildcard, and Joanna Mason's claim could be useful if she settles in midfield and delivers a clean run.

runners_data.name: Sands Of Seve
runners_data.note: Off 57 days and wearing a visor, Gary Harrison's three-year-old won over 5f on standard and placed on soft but has no good-going win on the board — 0W0P on sim going raises a stamina-speed query on this surface; a true hold-up horse squeezed forward on the map, he is unlikely to get the race run to suit.

runners_data.name: What A Tahoo
runners_data.note: Richard and Peter Fahey's in-form three-year-old won over 5f on good and has placed repeatedly, returning in good nick after 13 days with Cam Hardie in the saddle; his natural closer's style is compromised here by the crowded rear, yet his recent good-going record (1W3P) makes him the most dangerous of the hold-up group if he threads through.

runners_data.name: Bonito Cavalo
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old veteran for Jim Goldie carrying a ⚠ fade-in-finish flag, returning after 78 days and with a dire sim-going record of 0W0P from 15 runs; despite a hold-up style naturally suited to stalking, his finishing effort has been chronically weak and the long lay-off adds further doubt.

runners_data.name: Sixcor
runners_data.note: Linda Perratt's eight-year-old has the best sim-going sample in the field (10/15, 1W6P) and David Allan takes the ride, giving him a solid course-profile angle; he is a true closer pushed into a midfield slot by the overcrowded rear, and while his consistency on good ground is a positive, his age and modest OR of 45 cap his ceiling.

runners_data.name: Hard Nut
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old for Linda Perratt ridden by apprentice Tom Kiely-Marshall, returning 8 days after his last run; historical good-going form shows a win and two places (1W2P) but his last five finishes include three sevens and a twelve, and at this age the regression pattern is hard to ignore.

races.paceDynamic: Wee Mary is the confirmed pace-setter here, likely to stride clear from the front on her own terms over this flat 5f at Musselburgh on good ground, creating a steady, sustainable gallop rather than a gruelling test. With only one horse anchoring the lead and the remainder of the field dominated by hold-up types who prefer to close from off the pace, this sets up as a race where the front end is not under serious pressure — a tactical gift for Wee Mary's connections, though her STYLE_FIT tag flags she is a promoted prominent type rather than a natural front-runner. The field contains considerably more genuine hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate at the rear: Auntie Jo, Sands Of Seve, What A Tahoo, Bonito Cavalo, Sixcor and Hard Nut are all true closers, and most will be forced to race closer to the pace than they prefer, compressing the midfield and leaving those at the very back with limited ground to make up in five furlongs. This race shape strongly favours horses that can race prominently or sit just off the leader and pounce in the final furlong, since true hold-up runners will have nowhere near enough time or ground to close effectively on a leader who is never seriously pressed.

watchPoints.text: Wee Mary (front) and the entire closing pack — if the hold-up horses (Auntie Jo, What A Tahoo, Sands Of Seve, Sixcor) all break slowly and find each other's heels in a 5f sprint, they will have no room to mount a challenge and Wee Mary could steal this unchallenged.

What A Tahoo — Cam Hardie must find a path through a congested midfield inside five furlongs; if he meets traffic at the 2f pole his strong recent form will count for nothing, making his draw and early positioning critical.

Bonito Cavalo — the 78-day absence combined with a flagged tendency to fade in the finish makes him a race-to-watch liability rather than a serious market mover; monitor for market drift as a sign connections are not confident.

Sands Of Seve — the visor is on for the first time according to headgear tag (hg:v), which could sharpen early speed and mean he travels closer to the pace than his hold-up profile suggests; watch for a surprise prominent run that changes the complexion of the midfield.

Data Fata Secutus — hg:p (probably hood/blinkers) and a recent 2nd on good going for Tudhope makes him worth tracking in running; if he improves for headgear and sits handy rather than deep, he could be Wee Mary's most immediate threat.
